what_changed: Accuracy 0.06 -> 0.18 (output-marginal learning); per-unit CKA of mass class means at the block 0.36 -> 0.71; mass decodable at the value token kappa 0.53 (embedding identity), not causal anywhere (all IIA ~0.09). Group-gradient agreement: unit-1 mass examples conflict with unit 0 (attn2 +0.20, mlp_in +0.20, mlp_out +0.13) while unit 2 agrees with unit 0 (+0.46-0.49).
hypothesis: Unit 1 (scale 5) receives gradients that pull the shared weights in a different direction from units 0 and 2; if this conflict persists, unit 1 will form its own mass route at formation (as in the seed-700 precursor), i.e. gradient conflict precedes and predicts a representational split.
evidence: Observation: unit-1 gradient cosine with unit 0 is 0.13-0.28 vs 0.46-0.56 for unit 2, across all tensor groups. Correlation only; no representation exists yet. Speculation: the seed-700 split also involved unit 1 (different seed, different network). Head relocation events at this step are a matching artifact (near-uniform attention; heads indistinguishable), not real relocations.
key_question: Is the unit-1 gradient conflict a stable property of the task (unit 1 needs a different conversion) or transient noise of early training?
best_experiment: Track u0~u1 vs u0~u2 gradient agreement and per-unit CKA (pairwise) over steps 200-900; if conflict persists and per-unit CKA for unit 1 drops at formation, the hypothesis is supported.
intervention_rationale: Early phase: no causal representation (block IIA 0.09), nothing to organize; edits at this stage were rejected or ineffective in the precursor (doc 27).

what_changed: Accuracy 0.18 -> 0.24, block IIA 0.09 -> 0.14 (still not causal). Matched panel: equivalent pairs are closer at the block (cos 0.998) than different-mass pairs (0.949) or different-acceleration pairs (0.933). Group-gradient pattern flipped: unit 0 vs unit 2 now orthogonal (-0.03 to +0.01), unit 1 agrees weakly with both (+0.15 to +0.27). MLP: 102 neurons in the M*A (product) family, 47 answer-F family (none causally important yet).
hypothesis: (a) The step-100 unit-1 conflict was transient optimisation noise, not a stable property (refuted as a stable effect). (b) A unit-invariant (canonical) mass geometry exists in the block BEFORE the block is causally used: decodability-before-causality.
evidence: Observation: gradient cosines changed sign/ranking between 100 and 200 (transient). Observation: equivalent-pair block cosine 0.998 vs other-mass 0.949. Correlational only; block IIA 0.14, so the geometry is not yet used. Product-family neurons: eta^2 selectivity only (no ablation effect).
key_question: When the block becomes causal (IIA >= 0.5), does it keep this equivalence-preserving geometry (shared code across units) or does it split into unit routes as in the seed-700 network?
best_experiment: Track equivalent vs other-mass block distance on the matched panel, per-unit-pair CKA, and the interaction share through the formation window; compare with the moment IIA crosses 0.5.
intervention_rationale: Early phase; the only eligible targets are iia/ood_dev and there is no causal code to strengthen; the precursor showed early edits fail S2 and do not create codes faster than training.

what_changed: Loss plateau: accuracy 0.243 (+0.005), block IIA 0.15. Equivalent input pairs now receive the same prediction 0.90 of the time (0.52 at step 200), while block geometry keeps equivalents closer (cos 0.998) than other masses (0.940). Per-unit CKA 0.96. Gradient groups re-converged for units 0/2 (+0.25 to +0.38); unit 1 is again the outlier in attn2 (+0.01) and mlp_out (+0.00). attn2.h1 alone reduced the IIT loss this interval (-0.023).
hypothesis: The network's OUTPUT already respects mass equivalence (same answer for the same canonical mass) before mass is causally localised in the block; equivalence is computed somewhere other than the block at this stage (candidate: the MLP reading layer-1/attn2 features). Unit-1 gradient conflict recurs in attn2/mlp_out specifically (oscillating, not monotone).
evidence: Observation: equivalent-pair agreement 0.90 at 24% accuracy (the answer distribution is not constant: accuracy is above the 1/13 chance and OOD differs). Correlational: block equivalence geometry. Causal: none yet (block IIA 0.15, all heads ~0.07).
key_question: Where is equivalence computed during the plateau, if not causally in the block?
best_experiment: Interchange at dims 16-63 and at layer-1 tokens for M on OBS (patch tool) at the next checkpoint where IIA moves; if neither carries M causally, equivalence agreement is driven by coarse output statistics rather than a mass variable.
intervention_rationale: Early phase, plateau; no causal target to strengthen, and formation-window edits are better informed once the code appears.

what_changed: Block interaction share jumped 0.05 -> 0.36 while per-unit CKA rose to 0.996; acceleration became more separable at the block (other-acc cosine 0.928 -> 0.971, i.e. the block now IGNORES acceleration more). MLP: mass-family neurons appear (M 20, A 12) alongside m/a input families; the product family shrank 83 -> 40. attn2.h1 again the main IIT-loss reducer (-0.033).
hypothesis: (1) The interaction jump with near-perfect per-unit CKA means the units share the SHAPE of the mass configuration but at unit-specific offsets/rotations: a route split can begin invisibly to CKA. (2) The 0.88-0.90 equivalent-pair agreement is not evidence of a mass variable: it reflects coarse output statistics (zero-status), because nothing is causally used yet.
evidence: Causal (Level 2, OBS interchange): acceleration at its layer-1 tokens 0.059, output factor S at dims 16-63 0.064, mass at its layer-1 tokens 0.068, block 0.153 -> no variable is causally used anywhere (all near the chance-like floor). Observation: CKA is rotation/scale invariant by construction, interaction is not; both measured on OBS. Speculation: zero-status explanation of equivalence agreement (to be checked once accuracy rises above the zero-case share).
key_question: Is the rising interaction an early unit-specific rotation that will become the formation-time route split, or noise in a block that still carries little mass variance?
best_experiment: Watch interaction and pairwise per-unit CKA after normalising for mass-variance magnitude; the onset of causal IIA will show whether the split carries into the causal code.
intervention_rationale: Early phase and no causal variable exists (Level-2 tests); an interaction-removal edit now would act on noise and is not eligible (early-phase targets are iia/ood_dev only).

what_changed: Plateau continues (acc 0.254, IIA 0.159). Group-gradient conflict has disappeared: all mass-unit pairs agree +0.31 to +0.51 in every tensor group. Interaction share 0.36 -> 0.40; mass-unit identity consolidated in the block (mu@block). Pooled edit and copy both 0.10 (chance-like).
hypothesis: The lineage engine's head 'relocations' since step 100 are matching artifacts: layer-1 heads 1 and 3 have near-identical role-attention signatures, so the Hungarian assignment swaps them while still reporting 'confident' (cosine >= 0.8) matches. The registered confidence rule lacks a margin criterion.
evidence: Level 2 (feature records): B-he-0002 alternates attn1.h1 / attn1.h3 at steps 0-500 with match cosines 0.977-0.998, all labelled 'confident'; B-he-0006 alternates attn1.h1/h2/h3 (0.92-0.99). Same swaps in A. This is a property of the matcher, not of the network.
key_question: How much of the lineage-event stream is matching ambiguity rather than real change, and how should it be reported?
best_experiment: Post hoc (report, disclosed): for every head/cluster match compute the best-vs-second-best similarity margin from stored evidence; flag matches with margin < 0.05 as ambiguous and exclude their relocation events from claims. The registered matcher keeps running unchanged so records stay consistent.
intervention_rationale: Early phase; no causal code. The finding concerns the measuring instrument, not the network.

what_changed: Mass multiplicative (discrete-log) character at h rose 0.35 -> 0.47, the first sign of the circular calculator code; equivalent-pair block cosine dropped 0.996 -> 0.990 and different-mass 0.931 -> 0.918 (mass separation growing); interaction 0.40 -> 0.30. Accuracy flat 0.246, IIA 0.166. Gradient groups agree (+0.13 to +0.48).
hypothesis: Formation is approaching: in the seed-700 network the discrete-log circle formed 1-2 checkpoints before block IIA rose (doc 25). Prediction (falsifiable): block IIA(M) will exceed 0.3 within 300 steps and the multiplicative character will exceed 0.7 before or with it.
evidence: Observation: mult-char trajectory 0.60 (100) -> 0.45 -> 0.40 -> 0.39 -> 0.35 -> 0.47; precursor pattern from doc 25 (different seed, correlation only). No causal change yet (all IIA 0.07-0.17).
key_question: Will the circle form before causal use again (a reproducible ordering across seeds), and will the route split accompany it?
best_experiment: Keep the Level-1 audit; at the first checkpoint with block IIA >= 0.3 run the head anatomy inspection (which heads write mass, per-unit CKA per head) to compare with seed 700's head-0/head-2 story.
intervention_rationale: Early phase; prediction registered above so that the formation-window decision can be judged against it.

what_changed: Silent reorganisation: behaviour flat (acc 0.239, IIA 0.176) while weights moved fast (relative change per 100 steps: attn1.qkv 0.46, W_out 0.43, attn2.qkv 0.37, attn1.o 0.35, the largest so far); MLP neuron identities churned (stable 19 vs 94 at 600, relocated 36). Block now separates masses (other-mass cosine 0.918 -> 0.848) and accelerations (0.972 -> 0.902). Route@block and A@mlp consolidated. Mult-char at h fell back 0.47 -> 0.34.
hypothesis: The network is rebuilding its internal basis on the plateau (large, coordinated weight motion with no behavioural change) before formation; the loss landscape is flat here, so this phase is not an edge-of-stability phase.
evidence: Observation: weight-update magnitudes and neuron-identity churn. Level 2 (Hessian power iteration on the training objective): sharpness 15.1, Adam-preconditioned 10.4 vs edge 2/lr = 1,001 -> two orders of magnitude below the edge. My step-600 prediction (circle before causal use, IIA > 0.3 by 900) is weakened by the circle's fall but not yet falsified.
key_question: Is the reorganisation leading toward formation (a causal mass code) or is the plateau extending?
best_experiment: Next checkpoint: block IIA, copy and mult-char together; if IIA rises with weight motion slowing, formation has started.
intervention_rationale: Early phase (IIA 0.18); rapid basis rotation means any edit now targets a transient basis.

what_changed: Plateau extends: acc 0.243, IIA 0.158 (-0.018). Mult-char at h fell again 0.34 -> 0.27; interaction rebounded 0.23 -> 0.41; weight motion slowed (attn1 no longer in the top updates; W_out 0.25). Equivalent-pair prediction agreement fell to 0.54 (from 0.77).
hypothesis: The step-700 basis rotation did not initiate formation; seed 701 has a longer plateau than seed 700. My step-600 prediction (IIA > 0.3 by step 900, circle first) is now likely to fail; the circle's rise at 600 was a fluctuation, not a precursor.
evidence: Observation: three consecutive checkpoints of falling mult-char (0.47, 0.34, 0.27) with flat IIA. The equivalence-agreement drop (0.77 -> 0.54) together with flat accuracy supports the step-400 reading that this metric reflects coarse output statistics, not a mass variable.
key_question: What is the network learning during the plateau, if not mass? Candidate: the answer distribution conditioned on zero-status and the output unit.
best_experiment: At 900, check F decodability at the MLP and acceleration/product families against accuracy; a rise in F kappa without IIA would mean output-side learning precedes the mass variable.
intervention_rationale: Early phase. The only eligible targets would be iia/ood_dev; nothing indicates a code that a small edit could strengthen.

what_changed: Plateau persists (acc 0.249, IIA 0.159); my step-600 prediction (IIA > 0.3 by 900) is FALSIFIED. Mass decodability at the value token consolidated (kappa 0.50); answer F not decodable in the MLP (0.076). One MLP cluster split (B-ne-0046).
hypothesis: The plateau is a degenerate partial solution, not a wrong algorithm: the network detects zero answers and otherwise emits constants; it has not broken the symmetry needed to use mass or acceleration. It is not the doc-12 sign-ambiguity trap.
evidence: Level 2 (new read-only predictions tool, disclosed): predicts 0 for exactly the 17.7% of OBS questions whose answer is 0 (228/228), and otherwise mostly 8 (678) and 12 (241); agreement with F 0.249, with -F 0.228 (not a sign trap), with unit-ignoring variants 0.25 (chance-level after zeros); discrete-log agreement with F modulo 2/3/4/6 = 0.49/0.31/0.25/0.15 = chance -> no coarse multiplicative structure either.
key_question: Will the network escape the zero-plus-constant plateau on its own (as other mass_only seeds did), and does escape happen through the mass block or elsewhere?
best_experiment: Keep the predictions tool in the routine at each checkpoint until accuracy leaves 0.25; record which candidate function first rises above chance (F, a unit-ignoring variant, or the product without the output unit).
intervention_rationale: Nothing to reorganize: no mass, acceleration or calculation is used. Pushing the network off the plateau would be extra optimisation (the spec forbids crediting it to supervision); the precursor showed early edits fail behaviour-preservation. Decision: observe.

what_changed: Output distribution diversified (predictions now spread over 0, 5, 12, 3, 7 instead of mostly 8): accuracy 0.267 (+0.017). Equivalence geometry in the block is eroding: equivalent-pair cosine 0.975 -> 0.943 (different masses 0.840). Mass decodable in the block rising slowly (kappa 0.19 -> 0.22); attn2.qkv and attn2.o now among the largest updates.
hypothesis: The network has started to move off the zero-plus-constant solution by spreading its nonzero answers, but not yet by using mass: the block's early shared (unit-invariant) geometry is being dissolved before a causal code exists, i.e. symmetry breaking happens first in the readout/answer distribution.
evidence: Observation: prediction histogram changed; all candidate-function agreements stay within ~0.02 of the zero-plus-chance baseline (F 0.267, acc-unit-ignored 0.268, log mod 4 0.264 vs 0.25) -> no specific function yet. Causal: block IIA 0.167, layer-1 0.096, heads 0.07 (none used).
key_question: Which candidate function will rise above baseline first, and does the shared block geometry need to dissolve before the causal mass code can form?
best_experiment: Continue predictions + matched-panel tracking; when any agreement exceeds the 0.25 baseline by >= 0.05, run the head anatomy to locate the first causal writer.
intervention_rationale: Still early phase with no causal code; the change is in the answer distribution, which an edit would only perturb.
